card.name: Fakanau
card.profile: Fakanau (meaning "spells") is a traditional Tuvaluan male dance-song from Niutao and Nukufetau, performed seated or standing without moving from the spot, the story told through arm and upper-body gestures while an elder kept time at the circle’s center. Composed to praise an aliki or toa and to celebrate canoe-building and fishing, it was condemned as erotic and suppressed after Samoan London Missionary Society missionaries arrived from the 1860s, disappearing until its 1960 revival by ethnomusicologist Gerd Koch.
card.insight: Gerd Koch revived a fakanau on Niutao in 1960; it "became a rage, like pop music" and was filmed in 16mm that October. (Wikipedia, Fakanau)
